name: Windows/Linux laptop, no discrete GPU, 16 GB RAM (CPU + integrated graphics)
chip: x86_64 laptop CPU (Core Ultra / Ryzen class)
notes: The ordinary office or student laptop. Models run on the CPU (Ollama, llama.cpp, Atomic Chat all do this by default when no NVIDIA GPU is found).
Bandwidth is derived: 2 channels x 64-bit x 5,600 MT/s DDR5 / 8 = 89.6 GB/s (AMD lists 2 channels, DDR5-5600 / LPDDR5x-7500 for the Ryzen 7 8845HS). LPDDR5x-7500 laptops reach 120 GB/s.
Windows plus a browser takes 6-8 GB, so plan on about 8 GB for the model. 4-bit 2B-4B models are the comfortable size; a 4-bit 9B fits but is slow.
Expect single-digit to low-teens tokens per second for 4B-9B models: CPU decode is bandwidth-bound, and 89.6 GB/s is a third of an 8 GB laptop GPU.
